channel.title: koray.dev
channel.description: Koray Güler builds product at koative, an independent software studio in İstanbul. Notes on typed edges, small dependency lists and calm software.

item.title: Your LLM can't hallucinate a number it was never given
item.description: Anti-hallucination gets written as a prompt rule. It belongs in the code that builds the prompt, and the sharpest version of it is one line long.

item.title: Three bugs, one root cause: the label was not the identity
item.description: A rendering layer derives a human label from a machine identity. Both are strings. The type checker has nothing to say and the money path does.

item.title: Cache the prompt, not the inputs
item.description: The key listed the inputs someone believed mattered. The prompt had grown three fields since, and nothing in the system could have noticed.

item.title: The endpoint that succeeded at doing nothing
item.description: Correct status code, clean logs, zero exceptions, wrong data. What happens to the promise you deliberately didn't await.

item.title: I put a signing key in the browser on purpose
item.description: What that buys, split by what the attacker can already do, and why the property that actually protects the user is not in my code at all.

item.title: We built a distributed page cache, then deleted it
item.description: Three rounds of tuning to cut the write bill, then removal. The same machinery stayed for images.

item.title: Your error handler is inside the cache
item.description: A container restart took thirty seconds. The site stayed broken for an hour after it came back.

item.title: A missing capability beats a threshold
item.description: A limit can be misconfigured, and mine throttled the one thing that was supposed to recover from the problem it was throttling.

item.title: Idempotent writes don't make side effects idempotent
item.description: The upsert was the easy half. The write also caused four other things, and none of them were idempotent for free.

item.title: Math.floor is not a floor
item.description: The obvious fix drops a step. The clever fix rounds past the input. Neither raises an exception, and only one of them spends money you don't have.
